name: Herne

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Herne is a figure of British folklore. Shakespeare wrote about him in The Merry Wives of Windsor. In that play Herne is a hunter who hanged himself from an oak tree. He was then forced to haunt the woods where he died. Herne the Hunter appears in many legends. He is shown as a horned spirit. He may have begun as a woodland deity like Cernunnos. One tale from Windsor Forest describes Herne in fairy language. He shot intruders with invisible darts. He did this when they entered magical places.
objective: Document Herne the Hunter, the horned spirit of British folklore.
key_results: Record his origin in Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor.
Describe his form as a horned spirit and the possible Cernunnos link.
Note the Windsor Forest tale of invisible darts against intruders.
